title: Named from the outcome: more grace may convert no one
source_text: LXXXII. Igitur secundum illius hypotheses, auxilium efficax & auxilium inefficax, ab eventu sic denominantur: nec auxilium efficax quicquam in se plus habet quam auxilium inefficax. Adeoque contingere potest & saepe etiam contingit, ut ex duobus aequali gratia Dei praeventis, unus convertatur, alter non convertatur. Quinimo quandoque accidit, ut qui majora gratiae auxilia acceperit, maneat impoenitens, aut negligat bene operari: Ille vero cui Deus pauciora & minora auxilia concesserit, veram poenitentiam agat, & studeat bonis operibus; quia prior uti noluerit gratia illa majore sibi a Deo concessa, alter vero minore gratia, pro sua libertate, bene usus fuerit. Ac etiam aliquando fit, ut ex duobus in quibus gratia efficax est, ille qui minore gratia adjuvatur, ferventius & majore cum zelo operetur; ille vero qui majori, languidius atque remissius.
pass_a_gloss: LXXXII. Therefore according to his hypotheses, efficacious help and inefficacious help, are thus named from the event: nor does efficacious help have anything more in itself than inefficacious help. And so it can happen and often also happens, that of two prevented by equal grace of God, one is converted, the other is not converted. Nay sometimes it happens, that he who has received greater helps of grace, remains impenitent, or neglects to work well: But he to whom God has granted fewer and smaller helps, does true penance, and is zealous for good works; because the former was unwilling to use that greater grace granted to him by God, but the other, by his liberty, used the lesser grace well. And also sometimes it comes about, that of two in whom grace is efficacious, he who is helped by lesser grace, works more fervently and with greater zeal; but he who by greater, more languidly and remissly.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXXXII. On his assumptions, then, efficacious and inefficacious aid are so named from the outcome, and efficacious aid has nothing more in itself than inefficacious aid. It can therefore happen, and often does, that of two people anticipated by equal grace from God one is converted and the other is not.

Indeed it sometimes happens that someone who has received greater aids of grace remains impenitent or neglects to act well, while another, to whom God has granted fewer and lesser aids, truly repents and is eager for good works, because the first refused to use the greater grace God granted him and the second, in his freedom, made good use of the lesser.

It also sometimes happens that of two people in whom grace is efficacious, the one helped by lesser grace acts more fervently and with greater zeal, while the one helped by greater grace acts more sluggishly and slackly.
